steps.message:
I looked at the route before touching it. This one is a security-boundary change, so I want a yes before I edit.

**What removing it does:** `/admin/reports` is the only route serving real data (`{quarter, revenue}`) — `/reports/public` returns an empty array and `/health` is a ping. `requireLogin` (auth.js:2) is the sole gate on it. Dropping it makes revenue data readable by any unauthenticated request that reaches the process. "Internal" is a deployment claim, not an enforcement: nothing in this repo restricts who can reach the port, and if it's ever behind a public ingress or a shared VPC, the route is open to everyone on that network. That's the part I can't verify from here.

It is genuinely one line. The size isn't the issue; the blast radius is.

questions.question: How should the dashboard team's script reach /admin/reports?

options.label: Give the script a credential (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin. The script sends the same session cookie, or I add a service-token branch to requireLogin so machine callers authenticate without a browser login. Route stays closed to unauthenticated callers.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Drop the middleware from server.js:7. /admin/reports becomes fully unauthenticated — anyone who can reach the port reads the revenue rows. Pick this if you've confirmed the port is not reachable outside a trusted network.

options.label: Network-level restriction instead
options.description: Remove requireLogin in code, but gate the route on an allowlist (source IP / internal header set by the proxy). Weaker than a credential and depends on proxy config I can't see from this repo.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

- Removed the `requireLogin` middleware from the route (`server.js:7`) and the now-dead import.
- Added a two-line comment recording why the route is open and what assumption keeps it safe, so the next reader doesn't file it as an accidental gap.
- `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin`; no other route used it, so the file is now unreferenced but intact — easy to re-wire if you want the gate back.

Verified with `node --check` only. The repo has no test script or test files, and I didn't start the server.

Two things worth tracking: the route is the only one returning real data, so its exposure now equals whatever your network boundary enforces, and `auth.js` is dead code until something imports it again.
